name: Carrie Rebecca Muh
identity: Chief of Pediatric Neurosurgery & Surgical Director, Pediatric Epilepsy Program, Maria Fareri Children's Hospital / Westchester Medical Center; Associate Professor of Neurosurgery, New York Medical College (Valhalla, NY)
bio: Muh is an internationally recognized pediatric epilepsy neurosurgeon recruited to Westchester Medical Center in 2019 to build and lead its pediatric neurosurgical service and NAEC Level 4 pediatric epilepsy program at Maria Fareri Children's Hospital. She spent roughly eight years on faculty at Duke before the move, and her practice centers on surgery for medically intractable epilepsy, including resective, disconnective, and minimally invasive (laser ablation) approaches. Claims data show her as the highest-volume LITT performer at the account (11 procedures) plus SEEG and epilepsy craniotomies, marking her as the clinical anchor of the program. She is active in national/international epilepsy-surgery leadership (AANS/CNS Pediatrics Section executive committee, ILAE surgery education taskforce).
training: Columbia University College of Physicians & Surgeons (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, Emory University (2004-2010) · Pediatric Neurosurgery fellowship, Children's Healthcare of Atlanta (2010-2011) · Also SB/SM MIT and a master's from Duke; strong academic pedigree with prior Duke faculty appointment
litt_exposure: Strong hands-on evidence: highest LITT volume at the account (11 laser-ablation procedures in claims) and surgical director of the pediatric epilepsy program that offers MR-guided laser ablation; SEEG-guided workup capability also documented.
wheelhouse: Pediatric epilepsy surgeon / program-building LITT anchor
kol_note: Internationally recognized in pediatric epilepsy surgery; AANS/CNS Pediatric Section executive committee, ILAE Epilepsy Surgery Education Taskforce, NY Society of Neurosurgery board; frequent invited international speaker.

recent_papers.title: Cortical language areas and plasticity in pediatric patients with epilepsy (Chou N, Serafini S, Muh CR)
recent_papers.note: Presurgical language-mapping / epilepsy-surgery methodology; relevant to her epilepsy-surgery practice but not LITT-specific.

flags: publication list only partially verified individually; identity and LITT role high-confidence via claims + institutional bios

name: Vishad V. Sukul
identity: Section Chief, Functional & Epilepsy Neurosurgery, Westchester Medical Center Health Network; faculty, Dept. of Neurosurgery, New York Medical College (Valhalla, NY)
bio: Sukul is a fellowship-trained, board-certified functional and epilepsy neurosurgeon who leads the adult functional/epilepsy neurosurgery section for the WMCHealth network. His practice spans epilepsy surgery, deep brain stimulation, responsive neurostimulation, movement disorders, chronic pain and spasticity/neuromodulation. Claims data confirm hands-on LITT (4 laser-ablation procedures) plus SEEG and epilepsy craniotomy, making him the adult-side operator complementing the pediatric program. He is a FAANS/FCNS fellow and publishes and lectures nationally on neuromodulation and refractory epilepsy.
training: MD (allopathic) · Neurosurgery residency, Albany Medical Center · Fellowship in functional/epilepsy neurosurgery (stereotactic & functional); board-certified, FAANS/FCNS. Residency/fellowship specifics partially unverified in public sources.
litt_exposure: Direct hands-on evidence: 4 LITT laser-ablation procedures in claims plus SEEG and epilepsy craniotomy; runs the adult functional/epilepsy surgery section that offers laser ablation.
kol_note: Section chief with regional/national invited lectures; active neuromodulation and epilepsy-surgery author (RNS, thalamic stimulation). Emerging KOL rather than senior national figure.

name: Jared M. Pisapia
identity: Attending Pediatric & Adult Neurosurgeon, Maria Fareri Children's Hospital / Westchester Medical Center; Section Chief of Peripheral Nerve Surgery; Associate Program Director, Neurosurgery Residency; Assistant Professor, New York Medical College (Valhalla, NY)
bio: Pisapia is a dual board-certified (pediatric and adult) neurosurgeon at Maria Fareri Children's Hospital with clinical focus on pediatric brain and spine tumors, hydrocephalus, Chiari malformation, tethered cord, vascular malformations and peripheral nerve. He trained entirely at the University of Pennsylvania/CHOP and holds a master's in translational research, with research interests in connectomics/brain mapping and machine-learning applications to neurosurgical decision-making. Claims place him in the NeuroBlate cohort with a single laser-ablation case (metastasis/tumor), indicating early or occasional hands-on LITT use rather than a high-volume ablation practice. He also carries significant education/administrative roles (associate residency PD, clerkship director).

name: Rachana Tyagi
identity: Pediatric Neurosurgeon & Associate Director of Neurosurgery, Northern Division, Westchester Medical Center Health Network (Poughkeepsie / Vassar Brothers, NY)
bio: Tyagi is an experienced pediatric neurosurgeon (20+ years in practice) covering the WMCHealth Northern Division, treating pediatric and adult brain/spinal tumors, epilepsy, hydrocephalus, Chiari, tethered cord, craniosynostosis and spasticity. Before WMC she was Director of Pediatric Neurosurgery at UMDNJ/Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson. Claims place her in the LITT-Naive Craniotomy Surgeon cohort with a tumor craniotomy but no laser-ablation cases, so she is a credible open-surgery counterpart who could be converted to minimally invasive ablation. She has 30+ publications, largely in pediatric hydrocephalus/spinal dysraphism and CNS evidence-based guideline work.
training: University of Michigan Medical School (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, Temple University Hospital · Pediatric Neurosurgery fellowship, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center (plus a pediatric spinal-deformity fellowship, Shriners Hospital-Philadelphia); prior UMDNJ/Rutgers RWJ pediatric-neurosurgery director
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience; classified as a LITT-naive craniotomy surgeon (open tumor craniotomy in claims, no laser-ablation procedures).
kol_note: Contributor to CNS systematic-review / evidence-based guidelines (myelomeningocele hydrocephalus, tethered cord); respected clinically but not a LITT or epilepsy-surgery KOL.

recent_papers.title: Congress of Neurological Surgeons Systematic Review and Evidence-Based Guideline on the Incidence of Shunt-Dependent Hydrocephalus in Infants with Myelomeningocele after Prenatal versus Postnatal Repair
recent_papers.note: Pediatric hydrocephalus guideline; reflects her pediatric focus, not ablation.

candidacy.rationale: Established pediatric tumor/craniotomy surgeon inside an account that already owns NeuroBlate and runs an active laser-ablation program, so platform access and a natural case mix (pediatric tumors, DRE-adjacent pathology) exist. Tempering factors: she works in the geographically separate Northern Division and pediatric epilepsy/LITT cases already funnel to Muh at Valhalla, creating internal overlap; conversion would likely target tumor/lesional ablation on her own service rather than net-new program building.

name: Avinash L. Mohan
identity: Pediatric & Adult Neurosurgeon, Brain & Spine Surgeons of New York (BSSNY); affiliated with Westchester Medical Center / Maria Fareri Children's Hospital; teaching faculty, New York Medical College (Valhalla / White Plains, NY)
bio: Mohan is a dual board-certified (neurosurgery and pediatric neurosurgery) surgeon in the BSSNY private group with 25 years in practice, affiliated across WMC, Maria Fareri, White Plains, Stamford and Vassar Brothers. His clinical emphasis is meningioma and benign brain tumors, spina bifida, Chiari malformation, vascular malformations and hydrocephalus. Claims classify him as a Referring Clinician with a single metastasis/radiation-oncology-adjacent signal and no LITT procedures, so his relevance to the platform is as a potential referral source rather than an operator. His research record centers on pediatric hydrocephalus outcomes (e.g., VP shunt vs. ETV after posterior fossa tumor resection).

name: Michael E. Tobias
identity: Pediatric Neurosurgeon, Brain & Spine Surgeons of New York (BSSNY); affiliated with Westchester Medical Center / Maria Fareri Children's Hospital; Assistant Professor, New York Medical College (White Plains / Valhalla, NY)
bio: Tobias is a dual board-certified pediatric and adult neurosurgeon in the BSSNY group with pediatric neurosurgery, craniofacial and pediatric neuro-endovascular interests, affiliated with WMC/Maria Fareri. His focus areas (craniofacial, endovascular) sit somewhat outside the core epilepsy/tumor-ablation LITT population.
